# Control Narrative: Fire Water System (FWS)

Document: CN-FWS-001, Rev A (draft for client review). Date: 2026-10-18.

## 0. Corrections to the client draft

The draft gives the PLC control of the fire pumps. That conflicts with how listed fire pump controllers work (NFPA 20 practice). Three of its statements change. Confirm against the current NFPA 20, NFPA 25, and the AHJ or insurer requirements before issue.

| ID | Client draft | Corrected intent | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| CL-01 | PLC starts the fire pumps on low header pressure. | The listed controllers FPC-1 and FPC-2 start the pumps from their own pressure sensing. The PLC only monitors. | The start path must not depend on a PLC, network, or SCADA. A PLC fault must never block a start. |
| CL-02 | PLC stops the pumps after pressure recovers (SP-FWS-21). | No automatic stop in this scope. An operator stops each pump at its controller (SQ-FWS-02). | Pressure recovery does not show that the fire is out. A restart could be late or fail. NFPA 20 allows automatic stop only as a controller option, with a minimum run timer (SP-FWS-22), and only if the AHJ approves. |
| CL-03 | PLC trips FP-1 on low lube oil pressure and high coolant temperature. | Both are alarms only. The only automatic engine shutdown is overspeed, done by the engine and FPC-1. | A fire pump must run to destruction rather than stop on a protective trip. |

The client's pressure start points are accepted. They give a 10 psi gap between JP-1 and FP-2 and between FP-2 and FP-1 (SP-FWS-02 to 04).

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

The FWS keeps the fire water header pressurized and supplies fire pump water on demand. The PLC and SCADA scope is monitoring, alarming, and logging only.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-FWS-001 | The PLC shall have no output wired into the start or stop circuit of FPC-1, FPC-2, or JPC-1. | Inspect the I/O list and wiring drawings. |
| FR-FWS-002 | Loss of PLC, SCADA, or network shall not change pump start or stop behavior. | SAT: de-energize the PLC, lower the header pressure, and confirm that the pumps start. |
| FR-FWS-003 | SCADA shall not offer a start, stop, or setpoint-change command for FP-1, FP-2, or JP-1. | FAT: inspect the HMI. |

Interfaces: the listed controllers (hardwired), the fire alarm system (outside this scope), and SCADA.

## 2. Equipment and tags

The instrument index was not provided. The tags below are the ones this module uses. Tags marked * are assumed and must be confirmed (OI-03).

| Tag | Description |
|---|---|
| FP-1 / FPC-1* | Diesel fire pump (2500 gpm at 150 psi) / listed diesel controller |
| FP-2 / FPC-2* | Electric fire pump (same rating) / listed electric controller with ATS |
| JP-1 / JPC-1* | Jockey pump / its controller |
| PT-601 | Header pressure transmitter (PLC input) |
| LT-610 | FP-1 diesel fuel tank level |
| TT-615* | Pump room temperature |

Signals to the PLC are hardwired dry contacts from the controllers. Serial or network data may be added for diagnostics, but no alarm relies on it.

| Signal | Source | Type |
|---|---|---|
| FP-1 run, FP-1 fail to start, FPC-1 trouble (common), FPC-1 not in AUTO, FP-1 low oil pressure, FP-1 high coolant temp, FP-1 overspeed shutdown | FPC-1 | DI |
| FP-2 run, FPC-2 trouble (common), FPC-2 not in AUTO, FPC-2 power loss, FP-2 on alternate source (ATS) | FPC-2 | DI |
| JP-1 run, JP-1 trouble | JPC-1 | DI |
| PT-601, LT-610, TT-615 | Field transmitters | AI, 4-20 mA |

An electric controller may not provide a fail-to-start contact. The PLC therefore derives that alarm for both pumps (FR-FWS-020).

## 3. States and transitions

Pump states for FP-1 and FP-2 (ISA-106 style). The PLC observes these states and does not command them.

| State | Entry condition | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|
| S0 Off | Controller selector OFF, or source isolated | S1 |
| S1 Standby | Controller in AUTO, no trouble | S2, S3, S4, S0 |
| S2 Running (auto start) | Pressure fell below the controller start point | S1 (operator stop), S5 |
| S3 Running (manual start) | Operator start at the controller (test) | S1 (operator stop) |
| S4 Standby with trouble | Controller trouble active | S1 (trouble cleared), S2 |
| S5 Shutdown (FP-1 only) | Engine overspeed | S1 (manual reset at controller) |

| From | To | Initiator | Condition | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | S2 | Controller | PT sensing below the pump start point (SP-FWS-03 or 04) | Automatic |
| S1 | S3 | Operator | Start pushed at the controller | Manual |
| S2, S3 | S1 | Operator | Stop pushed at the controller | Manual |
| S2 | S5 | Engine/FPC-1 | Overspeed | Automatic |
| S5 | S1 | Operator | Manual reset at controller | Manual |
| S0 | S1 | Operator | Selector set to AUTO | Manual |

JP-1 is Standby or Running. JPC-1 starts JP-1 at SP-FWS-02 and stops it at SP-FWS-01 (automatic).

FR-FWS-004: The PLC shall show each pump state from the controller signals (S0 to S5). Test: FAT, force each input combination and check the display.

## 4. Regulatory control

| Loop | PV | Output | Action | Mode behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Header pressure | Controller pressure sensing | JP-1 start/stop | On/off, set in JPC-1 | Always automatic. No cascade or override. |

The PLC holds no control loop (FR-FWS-001). PT-601 is a monitoring input only. Pressure start points are settings in the listed controllers, and the values are in the setpoint list.

## 5. Sequences

**SQ-FWS-01 Pressure demand response** (executed by the controllers; the PLC monitors and alarms).

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | JPC-1 starts JP-1. | JP-1 run signal | SP-FWS-14 | Alarm AL-FWS-14. Pressure continues down to step 2. |
| 2 | FPC-2 starts FP-2. | FP-2 run signal | SP-FWS-13 | Alarm AL-FWS-04. FP-1 starts at its own point. |
| 3 | FPC-1 starts FP-1. | FP-1 run signal | Controller crank cycle (SP-FWS-20) | Alarm AL-FWS-03. Operator sends personnel to the pump room. |
| 4 | JPC-1 stops JP-1 when pressure recovers. | Pressure above SP-FWS-01 | None | Alarm AL-FWS-15 if JP-1 runs too long. |

Fire pumps that started stay running after step 4.

**SQ-FWS-02 Operator stop of a fire pump** (operator-prompted).

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Get incident command approval to stop. | Approval given | None | Do not stop the pump. |
| 2 | Check that PT-601 is above the JP-1 start point (SP-FWS-02) and stable. | Pressure stable | None | Keep the pump running. |
| 3 | Push STOP on the controller faceplate. | Run signal off | SP-FWS-18 | Alarm AL-FWS-16. Operator uses the controller local stop. |
| 4 | Set the controller selector to AUTO. | Not-in-AUTO signal clear | SP-FWS-19 | Alarm AL-FWS-07 or 08. |
| 5 | Check fuel level (FP-1) and clear controller trouble. | No active trouble | None | Raise a work order. |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

No chart was given. The rows are written here. PLC interlocks that stop a pump: none.

| Cause | Effect | Latched or auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP-1 overspeed | Engine shuts down (engine/FPC-1, listed). Alarm AL-FWS-10. | Latched | Manual reset at FPC-1 |
| FP-1 low oil pressure | Alarm AL-FWS-11 only. Pump keeps running. | Auto-reset | Condition clears |
| FP-1 high coolant temp | Alarm AL-FWS-12 only. Pump keeps running. | Auto-reset | Condition clears |
| FP-2 normal source lost | ATS transfers to alternate source. Alarm AL-FWS-09. | Auto-reset | Source returns |
| LT-610 low | Alarm only | Auto-reset | Refuel |
| TT-615 low or high | Alarm only | Auto-reset | Condition clears |

FR-FWS-005: The PLC shall not trip or stop FP-1 or FP-2 for any process or machinery condition. Test: FAT, force every alarm input and check that no output changes.

SIS functions: none in this module. If a site SRS covers pump-room fire detection, it stays outside this narrative.

## 7. Alarms

No alarm database was given. Priorities are provisional until rationalization (OI-07). P1 is high, P2 medium, P3 low.

| ID | Condition | Pri | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| AL-FWS-01 | FP-1 running | P1 | Check for fire. Call the emergency team. |
| AL-FWS-02 | FP-2 running | P1 | Same as AL-FWS-01. |
| AL-FWS-03 | FP-1 fail to start (controller signal or derived) | P1 | Go to FPC-1. Start manually. |
| AL-FWS-04 | FP-2 fail to start (derived) | P1 | Go to FPC-2. Start manually. |
| AL-FWS-05 | FPC-1 trouble | P1 | Find the cause at the controller. |
| AL-FWS-06 | FPC-2 trouble | P1 | Find the cause at the controller. |
| AL-FWS-07 | FPC-1 not in AUTO | P2 | Set the selector to AUTO. |
| AL-FWS-08 | FPC-2 not in AUTO | P2 | Set the selector to AUTO. |
| AL-FWS-09 | FP-2 on alternate source, or FPC-2 power loss | P2 | Check the normal power source. |
| AL-FWS-10 | FP-1 overspeed shutdown | P1 | Inspect the engine. Reset at the controller. |
| AL-FWS-11 | FP-1 low oil pressure | P1 | Do not stop the pump. Send maintenance. |
| AL-FWS-12 | FP-1 high coolant temperature | P1 | Do not stop the pump. Send maintenance. |
| AL-FWS-13 | LT-610 low (SP-FWS-08) | P2 | Order fuel. |
| AL-FWS-13A | LT-610 low-low (SP-FWS-09) | P1 | Fill the tank now. |
| AL-FWS-14 | JP-1 trouble | P2 | Repair JP-1. |
| AL-FWS-15 | JP-1 starts too often or runs too long (SP-FWS-16, 17) | P2 | Look for a header leak. |
| AL-FWS-16 | Pump failed to stop | P2 | Use the local stop at the controller. |
| AL-FWS-17 | PT-601 low (SP-FWS-05) | P2 | Check JP-1 and the header for leaks. |
| AL-FWS-18 | PT-601 high (SP-FWS-06) | P3 | Check JPC-1 pressure settings. |
| AL-FWS-19 | TT-615 low or high (SP-FWS-10, 11) | P2 | Check pump room heating or ventilation. |
| AL-FWS-20 | Bad PV (PT-601, LT-610, TT-615) | P2 | Repair the instrument. |
| AL-FWS-21 | Signal circuit fault (open or short) | P2 | Repair the wiring. |

FR-FWS-020: The PLC shall raise AL-FWS-03 or 04 when PT-601 stays below the pump start point by the margin (SP-FWS-12) with no run signal for the delay (SP-FWS-13). Test: SAT, simulate PT-601 with the pump isolated.

FR-FWS-021: The PLC shall raise each alarm in the table at its stated condition. Test: FAT, force each input or AI value.

## 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | Detection | System response | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| PT-601 bad PV | Out of range (SP-FWS-07) | AL-FWS-20. Derived fail-to-start alarms are blocked. Pumps unaffected. | Repair PT-601. |
| Wire break or short on a DI | Input module diagnostics | AL-FWS-21 and bad quality on the tag | Repair wiring. |
| SCADA-to-PLC comms loss | HMI watchdog | Stale-data banner. PLC keeps logging. Pumps unaffected. | Comms restored |
| PLC power loss | Not applicable | Pumps unaffected (FR-FWS-002). | On restart the PLC reads all inputs, re-evaluates alarms, and issues no outputs. |
| FP-2 normal source lost | FPC-2 signals | ATS transfers. AL-FWS-09. | Source returns. |
| Both FP-2 sources lost | FPC-2 power loss | FP-1 is the only pump. AL-FWS-09 and AL-FWS-06. | Restore power. |
| LT-610 fault | Bad PV | AL-FWS-20. Check fuel by hand. | Repair LT-610. |

Fail positions: the PLC has no outputs to pump equipment. Controllers and ATS fail as listed.

FR-FWS-030: After a PLC restart, the PLC shall re-evaluate all alarms from live inputs and shall issue no field outputs. Test: SAT, cycle the PLC power.

## 9. Operator interface

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Displays | Header pressure PT-601 with trend. State of FP-1, FP-2, JP-1. FP-1 fuel level LT-610. Pump room temperature TT-615. All alarms in Section 7. |
| Operator can | Acknowledge alarms. View trends and event log. |
| Operator cannot | Start or stop pumps. Change SP-FWS-01 to 04. |
| Prompts | On AL-FWS-01 or 02: "Check for fire. Call the emergency team." On AL-FWS-16: "Use the local stop at the controller." |

FR-FWS-040: The PLC shall time-stamp every pump run, stop, and trouble event in the event log. Test: FAT, check the log after forced events.

Operations shall sign off the states, prompts, and priorities (OI-06).

|---|---|---|---|---|

| SP-FWS-02 | JP-1 start | 155 | psig | Client. Set in JPC-1. |
| SP-FWS-03 | FP-2 start | 145 | psig | Client. Set in FPC-2. |
| SP-FWS-04 | FP-1 start | 135 | psig | Client. Set in FPC-1. |

| SP-FWS-06 | PT-601 high alarm | 175 | psig | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-07 | PT-601 bad PV limits | 3.8 / 20.5 | mA | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-08 | LT-610 low | 67 | % of tank | NFPA 20 two-thirds value. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-09 | LT-610 low-low | 50 | % of tank | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-10 | TT-615 low | 40 | °F | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-11 | TT-615 high | 120 | °F | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-12 | Derived fail-to-start margin | 3 | psi | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-13 | Derived fail-to-start delay | 20 | s | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-14 | Run signal debounce and JP-1 run confirm | 2 / 5 | s | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-15 | PT-601 low alarm on-delay | 10 | s | Provisional. Confirm. |
| SP-FWS-16 | JP-1 excessive starts | 6 | starts/h | Provisional. Confirm. |

| SP-FWS-21 | Client auto-stop recovery delay | 10 | min | Not used (CL-02). |
| SP-FWS-22 | Minimum run timer if AHJ approves auto stop | 10 (electric), 30 (diesel) | min | Not used. Contingent on OI-01. |

## 11. Open items

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Get AHJ or insurer agreement to manual stop only (CL-02), and to alarm-only FP-1 protection (CL-03). | Terminal fire protection engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-02 | Confirm that JPC-1 uses its own pressure sensing and that the PLC does not control JP-1. | Integrator | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-03 | Assign tags for the controllers and TT-615. Issue the I/O list. | Controls lead | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-04 | Get the controller vendor signal lists. Confirm which contacts exist (for example fail to start on FPC-2). | Integrator | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-05 | Confirm LT-610 tank capacity, pump room temperature limits, and engine vendor requirements. | Mechanical engineer | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-06 | Sign off states, prompts, and priorities. | Operations manager | 2026-12-04 |
| OI-07 | Rationalize alarm priorities (ISA-18.2). | Controls lead and operations | 2026-12-04 |
| OI-08 | Check start points and PT-601 range against the pump curves and the piping pressure rating. | Fire protection engineer | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-09 | Define PLC UPS runtime. | Electrical engineer | 2026-11-20 |

I did not check NFPA clause numbers or the current editions. Several values (marked "NFPA 20" or "Provisional") rest on my recollection of the code and need confirmation. The STE pass was applied to the procedural and requirement text.
